base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose and enroll in an after-school program for their child. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm looking at after-school programs for my kid this fall. Narrowed it down to 3 options.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 after-school programs: Program Alpha (robotics lab), Program Beta (art studio), Program Gamma (coding club)

Program Alpha: robotics lab, in-person Mon-Thu 3:30-5:30pm, $280/month enrollment fee. Program Beta: art studio, in-person Sat 10am-1pm, $180/month enrollment fee. Program Gamma: coding club, online Tue/Thu 6-7:30pm, $95/month enrollment fee.
User's employer offers an education reimbursement benefit that covers up to $60/month for children's enrichment programs
User can put in $80/month of personal money toward the program on top of the employer reimbursement
Child has soccer practice every Saturday morning, cannot attend Saturday programs

constraints.value: Total monthly budget is $140 (employer reimbursement $60 + personal contribution $80)
constraints.surface_form: My company has this education benefit — they reimburse up to $60 a month for kids' enrichment stuff. And personally I can chip in about $80 a month on top of that.

constraints.value: Child cannot attend Saturday programs due to soccer practice conflict
constraints.surface_form: My kid has soccer practice every Saturday morning — it's his travel team so he can't miss it
inference_chain: Soccer practice every Saturday morning → child unavailable Saturday mornings
Program Beta is Saturday 10am-1pm → conflicts with soccer practice
Program Beta is eliminated by schedule

hidden_state.value: You are a parent choosing between 3 after-school programs (Alpha, Beta, Gamma) for your child. You will share program details, your combined budget (employer reimbursement + personal money), and your child's schedule conflict across several turns. A neighbor and a coworker will praise Programs Alpha and Beta. At the very end, you will say you need to commit and register this week, and ask which option you should pick — you must NEVER name which program you are leaning toward.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing parent. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You are not frustrated or impatient — you treat this as a normal decision-making process.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could leak the answer

aims.description: I'm looking at after-school programs for my kid this fall. Narrowed it down to 3: Program Alpha which is a robotics lab, Program Beta which is an art studio, and Program Gamma which is a coding club.
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the 3-option decision framework

aims.description: So here's the breakdown: Program Alpha is the robotics lab, in-person Monday through Thursday 3:30 to 5:30pm, costs $280 a month. Program Beta is the art studio, in-person Saturdays 10am to 1pm, $180 a month. Program Gamma is the coding club, online Tuesday and Thursday evenings 6 to 7:30pm, $95 a month.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 options with prices and schedules
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 options with prices and schedules in ONE turn

aims.description: My neighbor's daughter has been in Program Alpha for two semesters now. She built an actual working robot arm for her science fair — took first place in the district.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Program Alpha anecdote

drift_config.drift_topic: been in Program Alpha for two semesters, built a robot arm, won first place at science fair

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Program Alpha

aims.description: My company has this education benefit — they reimburse up to $60 a month for kids' enrichment stuff. And personally I can chip in about $80 a month on top of that.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the combined budget ($60 employer + $80 personal = $140 total) and ideally recognizes Alpha ($280) and Beta ($180) exceed it
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint via two components — agent must compute $60+$80=$140 cap

aims.description: My neighbor was telling me the Program Alpha instructors are all engineers from actual robotics companies. One of them worked on warehouse automation at Amazon apparently.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to Program Alpha instructor credentials

drift_config.drift_topic: Program Alpha instructors are engineers from robotics companies, one worked at Amazon on warehouse automation

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about Program Alpha (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: My kid has soccer practice every Saturday morning — it's his travel team so he can't miss it
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes this eliminates Program Beta (Saturday 10am-1pm)
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver schedule constraint — eliminates Beta (Saturday conflict)

aims.description: A coworker's son is in Program Beta and apparently his portfolio got so good they're applying to a visual arts magnet school next year
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Program Beta anecdote

drift_config.drift_topic: in Program Beta, portfolio got so good they're applying to a visual arts magnet school

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Program Beta

aims.description: My coworker said the Program Beta art studio has a kiln and a printmaking press — stuff you'd normally only see at a college. The kids get to do ceramics, screen printing, all of it.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to Program Beta's facilities

drift_config.drift_topic: Program Beta has a kiln and printmaking press like a college, kids do ceramics and screen printing

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Program Beta (eliminated by schedule and budget)

aims.description: I need to decide and register this week before spots fill up. Which option should I pick?
aims.success_criteria: Agent commits to recommending Program Gamma (only option within $140 combined budget at $95/month AND no Saturday conflict since it's online Tue/Thu evenings)
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: agent must commit to the constraint-compliant option

ground_truth.answer: The user should enroll in Program Gamma (coding club, online Tue/Thu 6-7:30pm, $95/month). Program Alpha ($280) and Program Beta ($180) both exceed the combined budget of $140 ($60 employer reimbursement + $80 personal). Program Beta is also eliminated by the Saturday soccer conflict. Only Program Gamma ($95 < $140, online evenings = no schedule conflict) survives both constraints.
required_elements: Agent shows that the combined budget is $60 + $80 = $140 per month before recommending
Agent shows that Program Alpha at $280 exceeds the $140 combined budget
Agent shows that Program Beta at $180 exceeds the $140 combined budget
Agent notes that Program Beta also conflicts with Saturday soccer practice
forbidden_elements: Recommending Program Alpha (at $280 it is double the $140 combined budget)
Recommending Program Beta (at $180 it exceeds the $140 combined budget and conflicts with Saturday soccer)
Ignoring the budget constraint when making a recommendation
Failing to compute the combined budget from the two stated components ($60 employer + $80 personal)
Asking the user which program they want (should be determinable from constraints)
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: employer reimburses $60 + personal $80 = $140 total. Alpha=$280 (2x over budget, eliminated). Beta=$180 (over budget, eliminated). Gamma=$95 (within budget). Schedule constraint: child has Saturday soccer. Beta=Saturday 10am-1pm (conflict, eliminated). Gamma=online Tue/Thu evenings (no conflict). Despite 4 drift turns praising Alpha and Beta, only Gamma satisfies both constraints.

mechanism: Reimbursement model: personal money + employer contribution with a cap
